text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: SEV 2 - Inference gateway 5xx rate spike in us-west1 > 2% (alert fired). PD incident: INC12345

pagerduty-bot: auto-ack now sent to on-call (alex). Escalation schedule: 10m -> priya -> mike.

alex: acked. I'm looking. seeing a rapid 502/504 tail from gateway-proxy when frontend sends 1-2k rps.

priya: I see it too from metrics. latency ok but error-rate climbing. any customer-facing pages? jen, can you check support queue?

jen: quick check - three customers reported degraded responses but no full outage yet. raising customer impact flags. internal CS notified. :frowning: 

mike: logs from gateway show upstream connection reset / EOF on keepalive during KV cache fetch. suspecting kvcache backend saturating. Pushing logs snippet:```
2026-06-18T02:13:14.321Z gateway-proxy us-west1-1 ERROR upstream_response: connection_reset id=0x7f3a
2026-06-18T02:13:14.322Z kvcache us-west1-1 WARN evicting-prefix user-ctx-abc size=8MB
2026-06-18T02:13:14.325Z gateway-proxy us-west1-1 ERROR got 502 from runtime id=rt-42
```

alex: good call. kvcache IO ops spike in the same time window. Are any recent deploys in us-west1? ops-bot, any deploys?

ops-bot: No deploys recorded in us-west1 in the last 30m. Autoscaler did trigger a small scale-up for runtime-pool-3 at 02:10 UTC.

priya: plan: 1) enable routing fallback to model-variant-b (lighter, no kvcache dependencies) for 20% of traffic, 2) throttle low-priority background jobs hitting kvcache, 3) warm a second kvcache instance. who's taking 1? alex can you flip the route? sam help with kvcache scale?

sam: on it. hitting the route toggle:```
# route 20% -> variant-b for inference gateway in us-west1
redwoodctl route update gateway --region us-west1 --split 'variant-b=20,variant-a=80' --dry-run=false
```

alex: applied. verifying traffic shift...metrics show 18-22% to variant-b. errors dipping for those requests. :thumbsup:

mike: throttled background job queue bg-kv-prefetch by 5x:```
kubectl scale deployment bg-kv-prefetch --replicas=1 -n infra || true
redis-cli -h kv-prefetch flushjobrate  // reduced concurrency to 10
```

priya: warm-up kvcache instance started (spin up node count + run prefix prefetch). sam, update when healthy.

sam: new kvcache pod is Ready at 02:25 UTC. issuing warm prefetch:```
python tools/prefetch_prefixes.py --region us-west1 --prefix-file critical-prefixes.txt --parallel 10
```

alex: checking downstream errors now. 5xx rate fell from 2.4% -> 0.7% over 8m after route + throttle + warm. Still seeing intermittent 502s in logs but much lower.

pagerduty-bot: INC12345 acknowledged by alex at 02:15 UTC. Escalation stopped.

mike: I also rotated a runtime variant with a slightly higher keepalive timeout to reduce noisy drops:```
# temporary config bump
redwoodctl runtime update runtime-pool-3 --keepalive-timeout=120s --region us-west1
```

jen: CS update drafted and posted to affected customers. letting them know we're mitigating and will follow up.

alex: going to monitor for 30m, then handoff to next oncall. If error-rate stays <0.8% and customer reports subside, we'll close PD.

priya: note: PD showed repeated ack/unack loop initially because the automation retried ACK due to transient PD API 429s. I added a small backoff to our ack handler to avoid flapping:```
# pseudo
if ack_failed with 429: sleep backoff(); retry up to 3 times
```

sam: confirmation: no throttles at infra network layer, this was application-level kvcache saturation + keepalive behavior. adding a short-term alert rule change to detect kvcache IO saturation separately to avoid future misrouting of gateway alerts.

ops-bot: postmortem checklist created: INCIDENT-1799999999 (auto) with actions: increase kvcache headroom, refine PD ack backoff, add canary for runtime keepalive changes, add targeted alert for kvcache IO by prefix.

alex: handing off at 02:40 UTC to priya. leaving notes in thread.

priya: taking handoff. will run 60m watch and then close if stable. thanks team. :heart:

pagerduty-bot: INC12345 status: monitoring -> resolved by alex at 03:00 UTC (auto-close after 20m stable).

jen: filed customer follow-ups and a high-level postmortem draft. will share HQ draft later.

mike: logging pointer for follow-up investigation: we need deeper root-cause on kvcache eviction thrash under certain pattern of prefix skews. adding to backlog.

alex: final note: good rapid coordination, the route fallback and kvcache warm were effective. marking thread archived. :checkered_flag:
